issue.title: fix(mint): clean up pending proofs (NULL melt_quote) on mint startup
issue.body:
Follow up PR from https://github.com/cashubtc/nutshell/pull/839

Pending proofs created during swap operations are written to `proofs_pending` with `melt_quote = NULL`. If the mint crashes mid-swap, these proofs are never cleaned up, the existing startup check only processes proofs that have an associated melt quote (i.e. outgoing Lightning payments).

## Changes

Extend `_check_pending_proofs_and_melt_quotes` to also query and remove pending proofs where `melt_quote IS NULL`. These are safe to delete on startup because:
-  if the mint is starting up, no swap is mid-flight
- Only melts involve an in-flight Lightning payment, and melts always write a non-NULL `melt_quote`

- A migration (`m034`) performs a one-time bulk cleanup of any existing orphaned rows for upgrading mints.

- `migrations.py`: `m034` deletes all `proofs_pending` rows with `melt_quote IS NULL`
- `crud.py`: adds `get_pending_proofs_without_melt_quote` query
- `ledger.py`: startup routine now unsets orphaned proofs after processing melt quotes
- `tests`: four new tests covering the cleanup logic and the query

comment.body:
> @KvngMikey You introduce a background task that periodically unsets pending proofs with no melt id back to unspent. The problem with this is that an attacker could time this exactly to double spend ecash by sending two concurrent swap operations at the exact time the background task is running to do its cleanup. If they are lucky, this might happen:
> 
> 1. Request 1 sets proofs pending
> 2. Background task on the mint unsets them back to spent.
> 3. Request 2 sets proofs pending

@a1denvalu3, I don't think this issue stems from this PR, there is no background task running this cleanup. What was added is:

- A migration (m034) that runs once on upgrade to clear historically stuck proofs.
- A method `_cleanup_orphaned_pending_proofs` called once before `asyncio.create_task(_run_regular_tasks())` is ever created, at this point no swaps can be in progress and the mint hasn't opened its doors to any requests yet.

comment.body:
The connection limit exhaustion becomes more serious over time, analysis of postgres connections points clearly to nutshell. For further inspection I add the output of pg stats and the output:

```
SELECT pid, usename, application_name, client_addr, state, 
       now() - state_change AS idle_duration,
       query
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE state = 'idle'
ORDER BY idle_duration DESC;
```

outputs dozens of from nutshell IP:

69025	postgres	idle	00:01:45.905381	COMMIT;

What claude thinks:

All 50 connections are idle with last query being COMMIT;, idle for ~1–2 minutes each, all arriving in a burst at almost the exact same timestamp (~00:01:45). This is a classic connection pool that is not being returned/closed properly.
The pattern — dozens of connections all finishing a COMMIT at the same wall-clock moment — means one request or job triggered a burst of parallel DB work, all committed, but the pool never released those connections back. They're just sitting there occupying slots.
Likely cause: A worker/job queue, a cron task, or a bulk operation that spawned many concurrent DB connections and didn't tear them down.

issue.title: feat(crypto): migrate BDHKE to BLS12-381 (v3 keysets)
issue.body:
## Summary
This pull request introduces BLS12-381 cryptography into the Cashu protocol, enabling smaller proofs and paving the way for multi-signature schemes and batch verification.

### Core Changes
- Introduces `v3` keysets using the BLS12-381 curve.
- Adds multiplicative blinding logic (`Y * r`) to replace legacy additive blinding (`Y + r*G`).
- Replaces DLEQ proof requirements with BLS pairing verification (`e(C, G2) == e(Y, K2)`).
- Modifies wallet redemption and proof construction steps to unblind signatures cleanly and omit unneeded DLEQ verification logic.
- Maintains complete backwards compatibility with `v1`/`v2` (`secp256k1`) keysets.
- Implements comprehensive batch pairing verification for unblinded BLS signatures.
- Updates keyset ID generation format to utilize the `02` prefix for BLS keysets.

### Testing
- Updates the wallet and mint CLI tests to dynamically accommodate both `secp256k1` and `BLS12-381` logic.
- Adds `tests/test_crypto_bls.py` test suite specifically for deterministic hash-to-curve testing, verification of individual BLS protocol steps, and batched BLS pairing checks.

issue.title: fix(mint): clean up pending proofs (NULL melt_quote) on mint startup
issue.body:
Follow up PR from https://github.com/cashubtc/nutshell/pull/839

Pending proofs created during swap operations are written to `proofs_pending` with `melt_quote = NULL`. If the mint crashes mid-swap, these proofs are never cleaned up, the existing startup check only processes proofs that have an associated melt quote (i.e. outgoing Lightning payments).

## Changes

Extend `_check_pending_proofs_and_melt_quotes` to also query and remove pending proofs where `melt_quote IS NULL`. These are safe to delete on startup because:
-  if the mint is starting up, no swap is mid-flight
- Only melts involve an in-flight Lightning payment, and melts always write a non-NULL `melt_quote`

- A migration (`m034`) performs a one-time bulk cleanup of any existing orphaned rows for upgrading mints.

- `migrations.py`: `m034` deletes all `proofs_pending` rows with `melt_quote IS NULL`
- `crud.py`: adds `get_pending_proofs_without_melt_quote` query
- `ledger.py`: startup routine now unsets orphaned proofs after processing melt quotes
- `tests`: four new tests covering the cleanup logic and the query
